**County with the largest decline (2014 → 2020)**  

| County (City & County of Honolulu counts as a county) | Motor‑vehicle‑theft rate 2014 (per 100 000) | Motor‑vehicle‑theft rate 2020 (per 100 000) | Drop 2020 – 2014 |
|-------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|------------------|
| City & County of **Honolulu** | 364.1 | 2 628.4 | **2 264.3** |
| Hawaii (Big Island) | 486.5 | 2 002.3 | 1 515.8 |
| Maui | 367.3 | 2 057.7 | 1 690.4 |
| Kauai | 173.0 | 1 501.6 | 1 328.6 |

**Answer:** The City & County of **Honolulu** experienced the biggest drop in motor‑vehicle‑theft rates per 100,000 residents between 2014 and 2020, falling by **about 2 264 cases per 100 000**.

**Sources**

* 2020 motor‑vehicle‑theft rates: “Crime in Hawaii 2020” – 2020 rates for each county (2 628.4 for Honolulu, 2 002.3 for Hawaii, 2 057.7 for Maui, 1 501.6 for Kauai)【commentary 1】.  
* 2014 motor‑vehicle‑theft rates: “Crime in Hawaii 2017” – table showing 2014 rates for each county (364.1 for Honolulu, 486.5 for Hawaii, 367.3 for Maui, 173.0 for Kauai)【commentary 13】.
